title: A Skin Patch That Reads Your Pulse Without Electronics
paragraphs: Scientists in Norway have made a small patch that can measure your pulse. It has no battery, no wires and no electronics inside. They shared the work in the journal Advanced Materials on 29 October 2026.

The patch is made of soft silicone rubber. One side has a tiny pattern that changes colour when the rubber stretches. The other side sticks to the skin and was inspired by the suction cups of an octopus.

Each heartbeat makes the skin move a little. The patch stretches and its colour changes. A normal phone camera can see this change, so no special machine is needed. The patch can show your pulse and also how stiff your blood vessels are.

questions.q: Why does the patch change colour?
questions.a: Because the skin moves with each pulse and the rubber stretches.

questions.q: What animal inspired the sticky side?

questions.a: Its camera sees the colour change.
